newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat futures down, but less than Chicago.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat futures down, but less than Chicago.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures edged down on Friday but resisted the full extent of Chicago's overnight fall.

January 1997 fell 50 cents to A$152.00 a tonne in 22 trades, March 1997 also fell 50 cents to A$153.00 in 10 trades and May 1997 fell A$1.00 to A$156.00 in eight trades. Seventy five A$160.00 January 1997 call options also traded at A$2.40.
I would have expected a slightly bigger move," Brendan Hillary of ANZ Futures Ltd said. Friday's decline of about A$1.00 compared with Thursday's rise of A$3.00, he pointed out.
With the U.S. in a 20 cent trading range for the March contract between $3.81 and $4.00, a close outside that range was needed to give direction, Hillary said.
The U.S. market's early rise then its heavy sell-off at the close indicated it may fall to test the bottom again, he said.

"I think a lot of local players may be sick of playing yo-yos with the world market and are perhaps waiting for an actual break. If (it) broke $3.80 you would see our market come off quite a bit," he said.
"(But) while the U.S. is range-trading (Australia will) sit roughly around this level," he said.
